In [[number theory]], the '''gcd-sum''' function,<ref name="toth">{{cite journal |author=Lászlo Tóth |title=A survey of gcd-sum functions |journal=J. Integer Sequences |volume=13 |year=2010}}</ref>
also called '''Pillai's arithmetical function''',<ref name="toth"/> is defined for every <math>n</math> by

:<math>P(n)=\sum_{k=1}^n\gcd(k,n)</math>

or equivalently<ref name="toth"/>

:<math>P(n) = \sum_{d\mid n} d \varphi(n/d)</math>

where <math>d</math> is a divisor of <math>n</math> and <math>\varphi</math> is [[Euler's totient function]].

it also can be written as<ref>[https://math.stackexchange.com/q/135351 Sum of GCD(k,n)]</ref>

:<math>P(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d \tau(d) \mu(n/d)</math>

where, <math>\tau</math> is the [[divisor function]], and <math>\mu</math> is the [[Möbius function]].

This multiplicative [[arithmetical function]] was introduced by the Indian mathematician [[Subbayya Sivasankaranarayana Pillai]] in 1933.<ref>{{cite journal |author=S. S. Pillai |title=On an arithmetic function |journal=Annamalai University Journal |volume=II |year=1933 |pages=242–248}}</ref>

<ref name="kevinbroughan">{{cite journal |last1=Broughan |first1=Kevin |title=The gcd-sum function |journal=Journal of Integer Sequences |date=2002 |volume=4 |issue=Article 01.2.2 |pages=1–19 }}</ref>
